headline: The Wilton starter.
subhead: A national park, a pond beach, a 200-year-old farm and a train to the city. Swipe.

slides.title: Weir Farm
slides.text: Connecticut's only national park dedicated to American painting, about 60 acres. Ranger-led tours are free.

slides.title: Merwin Meadows
slides.text: A 17-acre park right in Wilton Center, with a pond beach for swimming in summer.

slides.title: Woodcock Nature Center
slides.text: About 150 acres on the Wilton-Ridgefield line, with boardwalk trails over red maple wetlands.

slides.title: Ambler Farm
slides.text: A town-owned farm about 200 years old. Open dawn to dusk all year, known for maple syruping and its farm stand.

slides.title: Metro-North
slides.text: Stations in Wilton Center and Cannondale. Grand Central is about 1 hour 35 minutes by train.

caption:
Wilton packs a national park, a pond beach, a 200-year-old farm and a train to Grand Central into one town.

1. Weir Farm: Connecticut's only national park dedicated to American painting, with free ranger-led tours.
2. Merwin Meadows: a 17-acre park in Wilton Center with a pond beach in summer.
3. Woodcock Nature Center: about 150 acres on the Ridgefield line, with boardwalks over the wetlands.
4. Ambler Farm: town-owned, about 200 years old, open dawn to dusk every day.
5. Metro-North: stations in Wilton Center and Cannondale, about 1 hour 35 minutes to Grand Central.
